Title: tanmoyk2/build-enterprise-agents-code-assist

Brief: The project "Build Enterprise Agents (APEX012)" describes a heterogeneous multi‑agent system that integrates ADK 2.0, LangGraph, A2A workflows, MCP, Vertex AI Memory Bank and Gemini Enterprise. It aims to enable code‑assist capabilities across enterprise environments by orchestrating multiple specialized agents. The architecture leverages LangGraph for dynamic graph‑based reasoning, ADK 2.0 for agent development, and Vertex AI for scalable memory and inference. Current public information indicates a prototype stage; performance metrics and security assessments are not publicly disclosed, and deployment details remain limited.

signals.title: GEPA-Curator: Curated Learning for Self Improving Agents
signals.content: Large Language Models (LLMs) are increasingly used in multi-turn agentic workloads that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, but agentic failures can also come from prompt weaknesses, harness limitations, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. We argue that such failures may not provide useful learning signal, and may even be harmful; and thus it is essential to curate which tasks are provided to the prompt optimizer for better performance. We introduce GEPA-Curator, a framework that augments the prompt optimizer to select which agent experiences should shape prompt optimization. In particular, GEPA-Curator consists of two components: task curation, which filters out tasks that are likely to provide noisy or unreliable learning signals, and prior success retrieval, which selectively retrieves past successful trajectories for a task and provides them as additional context to the prompt optimizer. We evaluate GEPA-Curator on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and $τ$-bench, using both Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 as optimizer models. GEPA-Curator matches or exceeds the mean performance of both baselines, with gains of up to 20.7% over GEPA and 21.2% over ACE.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 82. Freshness: source age 0.98d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: GEPA-Curator – Curated Learning for Self‑Improving Agents

Large Language Models are increasingly deployed in multi‑turn, agentic tasks that require sustained interaction with complex environments. Existing reflective prompt optimizers such as GEPA learn from failed rollouts, yet many agentic failures stem from prompt weaknesses, harness limits, stochastic execution, or noisy judges. Such failures may provide little or misleading learning signal. GEPA‑Curator addresses this by curating which experiences are fed to the optimizer. It comprises (1) task curation – filtering out tasks likely to generate noisy or unreliable signals, and (2) prior‑success retrieval – pulling successful past trajectories for a task and adding them as context. Evaluations on GoBrowse, ALFWorld, AppWorld, and τ‑bench using Gemini 3.1 Pro and Claude Opus 5 show GEPA‑Curator matches or exceeds baseline performance, achieving up to +20.7% over GEPA and +21.2% over ACE.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: GEPA‑Curator – التعلم المنقح للوكيلات ذاتية التحسين

تُستَخدم نماذج اللغة الكبيرة بشكل متزايد في مهام متعددة الجولات تتطلب تفاعلًا مستمرًا مع بيئات معقدة. محسنات التعليمات الانعكاسية الحالية مثل GEPA تتعلم من الفشل، لكن العديد من الأخطاء الوكيلة تنبع من ضعف التعليمات، أو قيود المنصات، أو العشوائية في التنفيذ، أو أحكام غير دقيقة. قد لا توفر هذه الأخطاء إشارة تعلم مفيدة بل قد تكون مضرة. يواجه GEPA‑Curator هذه المشكلة عبر انتقاء التجارب التي تُغذَّى للمحسن. يتضمن الإطار (1) تنقية المهام – استبعاد المهام التي من المرجح أن تولد إشارات ضوضائية أو غير موثوقة، و(2) استرجاع النجاحات السابقة – جلب مسارات ناجحة سابقة للمهمة وإدراجها كسياق إضافي للمحسن. أظهرت التجارب على GoBrowse وALFWorld وAppWorld وτ‑bench باستخدام Gemini 3.1 Pro وClaude Opus 5 أن GEPA‑Curator يطابق أو يتفوق على الأداء الأساسي، مسجلاً تحسينات تصل إلى 20.7٪ مقارنةً بـ GEPA و21.2٪ مقارنةً بـ ACE.

signals.title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis
signals.content: We explore how to build performant large language model (LLM) tool-use agents that complete complex, multi-step tasks. Specifically, we study how data composition in synthetically generated tool-use environments affects the training of such agents. To do so, we propose the SynthAPI pipeline, which explicitly controls the diversity of generated environments along the axes of tools, tasks, and the databases on which the tools operate. By systematically varying SynthAPI's generation controls in 458,752 tasks across 849 trained models of four different sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream tool-use agent generalization based on the scale and composition of the synthesized environments. These predictable relationships reveal several lessons for scaling tool-use agent data. As data budgets grow, scaling tool and database diversity becomes more effective than increasing the number of tasks, and increasing data complexity yields larger gains. Scaling according to these findings yields agents that outperform models trained on data from prior work in large-scale tool-use agent and synthetic environment generation across four evaluation benchmarks.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 80. Freshness: source age 0.98d.
signals.brief_en:
Title: Scaling Laws for Tool-Use Agents via Controllable Environment Synthesis

We investigate how to train large language model (LLM) tool-use agents for complex, multi‑step tasks. Using the SynthAPI pipeline, we generate synthetic environments with explicit control over tool variety, task types, and underlying databases. Across 458,752 tasks and 849 models of four sizes, we derive a scaling law that predicts downstream generalization from the scale and composition of the synthetic data. Key findings: with larger data budgets, increasing tool and database diversity yields greater performance gains than merely adding more tasks; higher data complexity also improves results. Applying these principles produces agents that surpass prior synthetic‑environment baselines on four benchmark evaluations.
signals.brief_ar:
العنوان: قوانين التحجيم لوكلاء الاستخدام الأداتي عبر توليد بيئات قابلة للتحكم

نستكشف كيفية تدريب نماذج اللغة الكبيرة (LLM) لتصبح وكلاء استخدام أدوات قادرين على إكمال مهام معقدة متعددة الخطوات. من خلال خط أنابيب SynthAPI، نُنشئ بيئات اصطناعية مع تحكم صريح في تنوع الأدوات، وأنواع المهام، وقواعد البيانات التي تعمل عليها الأدوات. بعد اختبار 458 752 مهمة على 849 نموذجًا بأحجام مختلفة، استنتجنا قانونًا للتحجيم يتنبأ بقدرة الوكلاء على التعميم بناءً على حجم وتكوين البيانات المُصنّعة. النتائج الرئيسة: مع زيادة ميزانية البيانات، يصبح تنويع الأدوات وقواعد البيانات أكثر فاعلية من زيادة عدد المهام؛ كما أن تعقيد البيانات يحقق مكاسب أكبر. تطبيق هذه الاستنتاجات ينتج وكلاء يتفوقون على النماذج السابقة في توليد بيئات اصطناعية واستخدام الأدوات عبر أربعة معايير تقييم.

signals.title: Can LLMs Uncover Hidden Physical Laws through Free Exploration?
signals.content: Scientific discovery often begins with an unexpected observation that prompts a new research question. In a world with altered physical laws, can large language models (LLMs) notice unexpected behavior, such as heavier objects falling more slowly, and discover the law through experiments without being told what to investigate? To evaluate this ability, we introduce LongChang, an automated framework that creates simulated worlds with altered physics, where one or more laws differ from ordinary physics. The evaluated LLMs act as explorers, manipulating objects and building tools to investigate their own questions without research tasks or hints about these laws. Separate LLM agents generate and review scenes, review tool designs, and evaluate reports for correctness and experimental support using the altered physical laws and exploration records. These records guide scene evolution for further exploration, allowing the full cycle to run without human intervention. Among 12 LLMs, GPT-6-Astra achieves a discovery rate of 16.7%, while the other 11 score 0%. The exploration records reveal uninvestigated anomalies and only partial identification of the altered physical laws.
signals.score_reason: academic/research signal; agentic AI relevance; large language model relevance; model capability relevance. Final score: 73. Freshness: source age 0.98d.
signals.brief_en: Brief: This study tests whether large language models can autonomously discover altered physical laws in simulated worlds. Using the LongChang framework, LLMs explore environments where gravity or other fundamentals differ, without any task prompts. Agents manipulate objects, design tools, and generate reports that are automatically reviewed for consistency with the hidden laws. Across 12 models, only GPT‑6‑Astra identified a law change in 2 of 12 trials (16.7% success); the remaining models failed to detect any deviation. The exploration logs show many unexplained anomalies and incomplete hypotheses, highlighting current limits in self‑directed scientific discovery by LLMs.
signals.brief_ar: ملخص: يختبر هذا البحث قدرة نماذج اللغة الكبيرة على اكتشاف قوانين فيزيائية معدَّلة في عوالم محاكاة دون توجيه بشري. يستخدم الإطار LongChang بيئات تُغيَّر فيها الجاذبية أو غيرها من القوانين الأساسية، وتُكلف النماذج باستكشافها، وتصميم أدوات، وإعداد تقارير تُقَيَّم تلقائيًا للتماشي مع القوانين المخفية. بين 12 نموذجًا، نجح GPT‑6‑Astra في التعرف على تغيير قانون في 2 من 12 تجربة (نسبة نجاح 16.7٪) بينما فشل البقية تمامًا. تُظهر سجلات الاستكشاف وجود شذوذ غير مفسَّر وافتراضات جزئية فقط، ما يبرز حدود القدرة الحالية للـ LLM على الاكتشاف العلمي المستقل.
